title: Aggression & Violence: Studies and Applications
welcome_lead: Meet Bandura's Bobo Doll and the social learning of aggression.
meta_desc: GCSE Psychology adventure on Bandura's Bobo Doll study and social learning theory of aggression.

walkthroughs.body_html: Bandura showed 3-6 year olds an adult acting aggressively (or not) towards a Bobo Doll. Children who watched aggression were more aggressive when given the doll later — and often copied specific moves. Shows aggression can be learned by observation.
Attention, retention, reproduction, motivation. We must attend to a model, remember the act, be able to do it, and have a reason (often vicarious reinforcement) to repeat it.

The media-violence debate asks whether watching violent TV or games increases aggression. Some studies find short-term effects; others find none. SLT supports concerns, but most psychologists argue effects are small and depend on other factors.
